stories.title: Liverpool owner FSG holds talks over buying majority stake in Cadillac F1 team
summary: Deal would be worth more than £2bnCadillac are jointly owned by Mark WalterLiverpool’s owner, Fenway Sports Group, has held talks about buying a majority stake in the Cadillac Formula One team for more than £2bn as Mark Walter continues to sell off his sporting assets amid allegations of insurance fraud.Cadillac entered F1 this year as a joint venture between General Motors and Walter’s TWG Global, which sold its controlling interest in the NBA’s Los Angeles Lakers and a 13% stake in Chelsea this summer, and is also looking to sell Los Angeles Sparks, the WNBA team.

stories.title: Has a footballer ever run a marathon faster than James Milner? | The Knowledge
summary: Yes, the bleep test-loving former Brighton, Liverpool and Manchester City player recorded an excellent time of 3hr 9min 4sec, an average of 7min 13sec per mile.

That very respectable time has now been surpassed by the Premier League’s record appearance maker, so we thought we had better take a gulp of our isotonic energy drink and run through a few more tales of football’s marathon men and women.

stories.title: Choke of the century? Chengdu collapse sets up thrilling Chinese Super League climax
summary: John Aloisi’s side need a point on the final day to seal their maiden title – but their form has dropped off a cliffWith four games of the Chinese Super League to go, Chengdu Rongcheng needed just a point to clinch their first title.
With one game to go, they still need a point.
What was a formality has become a formidable task.

stories.title: Qatar pulls out of hosting 2028 Nations Championship owing to Middle East crisis
summary: Title sponsorship with Qatar Airways also cancelledParis’s Stade de France most likely venue for 2028 finalsQatar will not host the finals of the 2028 Nations Championship owing to uncertainty caused by the war in the Middle East in a development that has also led to the cancellation of a planned title sponsorship deal for the new tournament with Qatar Airways.Following months of negotiations both parties have agreed to withdraw from an agreement that would have seen Qatar stage the six-match final series in 2028 and 2032, as well as a title sponsorship for four editions of the competition with the national airline.

stories.title: West Ham took too long to sack Nuno and now must trust Parker to do what he does best | Jacob Steinberg
summary: Forget speculation over how a Parker-led side would fare in the Premier League and let the man who has taken three clubs up do his work againIt has taken West Ham six months to come to their senses and sack Nuno Espírito Santo, but at least the decision has arrived early enough to revive their hopes of automatic promotion.Dithering was no longer an option after the dismal performance against West Brom last Saturday.

stories.title: Mainoo and Lacey raise the spirits but systemic change still required at Manchester United | Nick Ames
summary: There were protests at Old Trafford and even though two academy products stood out, Michael Carrick’s future is far from safeGreen and yellow balloons bobbed around the Stretford End.
United have led their supporters, remarkable in their tenor of backing for players and head coach here, up more than enough false peaks over the past 13 years.
Arguably, that is one reason for Carrick being given the job on a permanent basis.

stories.title: Lennart Karl steals in behind Atlético Madrid to inspire Bayern Munich win
summary: “This stadium brings back bad memories but I hope to be able to replace them with good ones,” Harry Kane had said on Monday night, and 24 hours later this was a start.
A small step, perhaps, towards coming back on 5 June and having a second go at winning the Champions League in the arena where he lost the 2019 final.
On his first European outing since winning the Ballon d’Or, the England captain was unable to score but he and his Bayern Munich team defeated Atlético Madrid, fellow semi-finalists from last season.

stories.title: Championship roundup: Devlin’s double for Portsmouth denies Swansea top spot
summary: Birmingham sink Millwall to keep up good formNorwich thump Rams and pile pressure on EustaceTerry Devlin’s double denied Swansea the chance to take top spot in the Championship as in-form Portsmouth won 3-1 at Fratton Park.Devlin’s first-half goal looked like it was going to be enough for Pompey but Zan Vipotnik, the Championship’s top scorer last season, won and converted an 85th-minute penalty to set up a blockbuster finale.

stories.title: Manchester United produce comeback for the ages as Cunha double floors Roma
summary: Michael Carrick enjoyed one of his finest nights as a Manchester United player in the Champions League against Roma, scoring twice in a 7-1 win in the quarter-final, second leg in 2007.
Amid an atmosphere of continued fan anger towards the United ownership, Carrick’s team had been implausibly bad.
Roma took a 2-0 lead into the break and the truth was that the scoreline greatly flattered United.

stories.title: USOPC considering plan to sell stake in Team USA as LA Olympics approach
summary: US set to host Summer and Winter Olympics USOPC CEO says business model in early stagesThe US Olympic and Paralympic Committee (USOPC) is in the advanced stages of setting up an entity to sell a stake ⁠in the commercial rights for Team USA in return for capital, according to multiple reports.Any deal would mark a significant shift for the USOPC, a non-profit organization that, unlike many national Olympic committees, relies heavily on sponsorships, licensing ⁠and other commercial revenue streams rather than government funding.

stories.title: Tenerife footballer Jesús de Miguel dies aged 30 after on-pitch collision
summary: The homicide division of the national police has opened judicial proceedings into a possible involuntary manslaughter, a routine procedure after any death not by natural causes.

The chief public prosecutor in Santa Cruz de Tenerife told the state news agency EFE that it was “very difficult” for a case to come to court.Tenerife announced that De Miguel had died at 8am on Tuesday after he had been taken into intensive care on Monday afternoon.
He did not regain consciousness after a cardiorespiratory arrest.
